def factor_tail_asymmetry_jump_severity(df):
    """Downside vs upside tail jump severity asymmetry using lagged realized vol."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    vol = ret.rolling(63, min_periods=20).std(ddof=1).shift(1)
    threshold = 1.5 * vol
    vol_safe = vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    valid = vol > 0
    down_cond = (ret < -threshold) & valid
    up_cond = (ret > threshold) & valid
    down_sev = np.where(down_cond, (-(ret + threshold) / vol_safe).clip(lower=0.0), 0.0)
    up_sev = np.where(up_cond, ((ret - threshold) / vol_safe).clip(lower=0.0), 0.0)
    down_sum = pd.Series(down_sev, index=df_copy.index).rolling(63, min_periods=20).sum()
    up_sum = pd.Series(up_sev, index=df_copy.index).rolling(63, min_periods=20).sum()
    df_copy["factor_tail_asymmetry_jump_severity"] = -(down_sum - up_sum) / (down_sum + up_sum + 1.0)
    return df_copy["factor_tail_asymmetry_jump_severity"]
description: Mutation preserves the parent's asymmetric tail jump mechanism but replaces binary jump counts with continuous magnitude severity: each tail exceedance contributes its excess return normalized by lagged realized volatility. This retains the same downside vs upside risk-aversion ordering while providing more linear signal for IC/ICIR, without adding a new feature family or cross-sectional transform.
